Hi Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have the same next steps and can land the benchmarking items: 

1) What we covered
- Primary use: real-time Q&A over indexed docs (avg prompt ~220 tokens, expected 6–8 reqs/sec peak per region)
- Target p95 latency target: <= 220ms for single-turn generation at 2k context (this is what your SRE asked about)
- Throughput sensitivity: you asked about max sustained requests per GPU and how throughput scales with batching and KV cache reuse

2) Action items
- Marissa will send the lightweight throughput readout and a short config note (I flagged the expected model family and quantization tradeoffs).
- Alex/Procurement: share preferred procurement timeline and whether we should include a Dedicated pricing estimate or stick with hosted for the POC.
- Ava: propose a one-hour bench window for the week of 4/12 where Redwood runs a small synthetic traffic run against the model you're evaluating.

I attached the readout Marissa prepared and a brief config note. If we can lock in the bench window now I’ll reserve a slot with Engineering. 

Thanks —

Alex — quick technical note based on the mini readout I ran after the call. High-level answers below; happy to jump on a short sync if you want the raw runbook.

- Per-GPU sustained qps (L2 family, 4-bit quant): warm-KV-cache steady-state ~28 qps for single-turn gen at 2k context; cold cache drops to ~9–11 qps until prefixes start reusing KV. These numbers are with continuous batching configured at target latency ~200–220ms.
- If you enable prefix caching for your most common prompts (you mentioned a small set of canonical workflows), we typically see effective throughput improve ~2.2x in production-like runs. That’s reflected in the attached CSV readout (columns: timestamp,qps,p95_ms,cpu,gpu_mem).
- Dedicated trial estimate: for a 3-day small Dedicated cluster (2 x A100-equivalent workers) expect order-of-magnitude cost in the SOW; Ava will follow up with a formal cost estimate.

Let me know if you want me to include a short section on tuning batching policy (inter-op vs intra-op) — that's where you can trade a few ms for significantly higher throughput.

-M
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
